text:
Sasha: @channel P0 page — multiple customers reporting high latency and 5xx errors on /generate in us-east. Alerting via PD INC-432. Symptoms: sudden KV cache memory growth on inference shards and throughput collapse. Seeing continuous-batching backlog. Anybody oncall take? :rotating_light:

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-432 created by monitoring. Linked runbook: /runbooks/kv-cache-regressions. Paging oncall: @Mike.

Lauren: ACK. Pulling heap dumps + runtimemetrics. Early observation: shard-3 KV cache size jumped from ~12GB -> ~52GB within last 10m. GC pressure high, OOM killers firing on a couple of pods. Stack traces show kernel fallback paths for attention kernels.

Mike: Taking this. Quick ask: was there any model or quantization rollout in the last deploy window?

Julia: Yes — there was an automated rollout last hour for the new AWQ-int8 path for model redwood/generate-3.2 on prod-us-east. Canary went green but looks like a perf regression for long-context traffic. AWQ's index layout increases per-KV footprint in some cases. Also looks like the runtime selected a fallback kernel that materializes larger KV tensors when sequence_len > 1024.

Lauren: Confirmed: kernel selection log shows fallback_kernel=matmul_fallback on several hot shards. That lines up with the KV size jump.

Sasha: Quick mitigation options I can push now: 1) disable continuous batching on the route, 2) reduce max_batch_tokens, 3) pin model to previous quant variant. Which is fastest?

Mike: Do 1 + 2 immediately (low risk). Plan 3 as a rolling rollback after stabilization. Lauren, can you apply route-level hotfix?

Lauren: Applying hotfix now — toggling continuous batching off and reducing max batch token budget for /generate in us-east.

Lauren: Command I ran:
```
# hotfix: disable continuous batching + reduce batch tokens
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://console.internal/api/routes/config \
 -d '{"route":"/generate","continuous_batching":false,"max_batch_tokens":4096}'
```

DeployBot: Route config change applied to /generate (prod-us-east). Change id: cfg-20240324-001. No rolling restart required.

Mike: Monitoring metrics... mem usage on shard-3 now dropping from 52GB -> 28GB. Latency improved but still above normal for some requests.

Julia: Good. While that's resolving, we should revert the quant path or pin to the previous GPTQ variant. AWQ-int8 seems to inflate KV for long prefix lengths because of extra index buffers. I recommend rollback to gptq-4bit variant for the affected model until we either adjust kernel selection or add a KV-compression optimization.

Sasha: Can you prepare the rollback command? We'll do a canary to 10% then full. Also need to coordinate customer comms.

Julia: Rollback payload (will pin variant immediately):
```
# rollback model variant to GPTQ fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://console.internal/api/models/redwood/generate-3.2/rollouts \
 -d '{"pin_variant":"gptq-4bit","rollout":10}'
```

Lauren: Initiating 10% canary rollback now. Watching memory and error rates.

DeployBot: Model rollout initiated: redwood/generate-3.2 -> pin_variant=gptq-4bit @10%.

Mike: Seeing error rate drop on canary subset, mem further trending down. Initiating gradual rollout to 100% over 10 minutes.

Tom: Customer impact summary for status page: approx 4 enterprise tenants experienced degraded latencies and transient 5xxs. ETA for full mitigation ~20-30m assuming rollback completes cleanly. I'll draft a brief status update and ping CS owners.

Lauren: Rollout at 100% applied. KV cache sizes returned to baseline across all shards (~11-14GB). GC pressure cleared.

Sasha: Nice work team. Quick postmortem notes we should capture in INC-432: root cause = quantization path (AWQ-int8) + kernel selection fallback that increases KV footprint for long-context; contributing factor = canary window too small for long-tail traffic patterns; mitigation = route-level batching limits, disable continuous batching, rollback model variant to gptq-4bit. Actions: enlarge canary window for model-level quantization rollouts, add automated KV size assertions to rollout checks, and add a runtime flag to prefer memory-efficient kernels for long prefixes.

Julia: I'll open the ML PR to add KV footprint tests and a preflight check that simulates long-sequence traffic patterns against any quant path. Also adding a telemetry counter for per-token KV size by variant.

Lauren: Ops action item: add a circuit breaker in console that auto-disables continuous batching for a route if per-shard KV > XGB or if mem growth rate > Y GB/min.

Mike: Oncall handoff: Sasha -> Eve for the night shift. Eve, I handed over the incident state, mitigations applied, and follow-ups in INC-432. Please monitor for 2 hours and escalate if any reappearance.

Eve: Taking handoff. I have the runbook and will watch the dashboard. If something pops I will wake the team.

Tom: Status update sent to customers and posted to status.redwood.ai — included note about quick rollback and that investigation continues.

Sasha: Closing PD incident after stabilization and customer notifications. Will schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow with eng-runtime, eng-ml, and eng-sre.

incident-bot: INC-432 marked RESOLVED by Sasha. Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2024-03-25 09:00 UTC.

Lauren: Quick log excerpt for the postmortem (copied):
```
[metrics] shard-3.kv_bytes: 12.3GB -> 52.7GB (t=+8m)
[trace] kernel_selection: default_opt -> matmul_fallback @ seq_len 1536
[deploy] model:redwood/generate-3.2 variant:awq-int8 canary->full @ t=+45m
```

Sasha: Thanks all. Filing follow-ups and closing thread. :thumbsup:
